name: Market Volatility
description: Increased market volatility – particularly in specific asset classes – can significantly impact technical analysis and fundamental analysis results, leading to inconsistencies.

name: News Events
description: Significant news releases (political, economic, industry-specific) can drastically alter market sentiment and trigger rapid changes in technical indicators.

name: Trading Volume
description: A sudden spike or drop in trading volume can influence the accuracy of technical analysis, especially when combined with market sentiment.

name: Order Book Dynamics
description: Changes in the order book – buy/sell pressure – can create spurious correlations or biases in technical analysis, especially if not properly understood.

name: Transaction Costs
description: Transaction costs (slippage, commissions) can introduce noise into the data and alter the relative importance of different indicators.

name: Time of Day
description: The time of day when the analysis is run can have a significant impact on the data – patterns may shift significantly.

name: Backtesting Data Quality
description: The quality of the historical data used to train the model significantly affects the results. Noise or biases in the data can manifest in unexpected results.

name: Model Bias
description: The model itself may be biased towards certain patterns or indicators, creating the impression of a problem.

name: Data Processing Errors
description: Errors in data cleaning or transformation can introduce irrelevant or misleading signals.

name: Market Segmentation
description: Different market segments may exhibit distinct patterns that are not reflected in a single model.

name: External Correlations
description: Correlation with external, often unobserved, events can be difficult to predict.

name: Data Sampling Bias
description: The sample data used for training might not be representative of the broader market.

name: Model Lag
description: The model might be lagging behind the actual market, particularly with complex, dynamic environments.

name: System Latency
description: The speed of the system can introduce delays or fluctuations that affect the results, even with minimal changes in the market.
